sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (EU establishment and services freedoms)
Belgium–Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) Bilateral Investment Treaty network
Luxembourg–China Double Taxation Agreement (1985, Article on international shipping)
OECD/G20 Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures (MLI)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme, as amended; Loi du 13 janvier 2019 relative au registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), as amended to restrict public access following CJEU joined cases C-37/21 and C-718/21 (Sovim); Règlement CSSF n° 12-02 du 14 décembre 2012 relatif à la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, as amended; Loi du 19 décembre 2002 concernant le registre de commerce et des sociétés et la comptabilité annuelle et consolidée des entreprises, as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / official excerpt of the commercial register of the ultimate corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of each foreign shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille certificate; consular legalization by the Luxembourg Embassy where the origin state is not party to the Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / certificate of active status of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or trade register of the foreign shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille certificate; consular legalization where applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO register extract of the corporate shareholder evidencing the full ownership chain to individual beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent beneficial-ownership registry of the foreign shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille certificate; consular legalization where applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (procuration) of each corporate shareholder and individual UBO authorizing the Luxembourg incorporation counsel and, where applicable, the Luxembourg notary to file the name reservation and sign the incorporation instruments
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction where the signatory is resident or the corporate deed is established
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille certificate; consular legalization by Luxembourg Embassy for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of the passports / identity documents of all individual beneficial owners and authorized directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public, national records office, or Luxembourg consular post in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy with Hague Apostille or consular legalization where required by the accepting Luxembourg professional

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory and continuous risk-based screening of every UBO, director, officer, and authorized signatory against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, Luxembourg CSSF and Ministry of Justice sanctions notices, and international PEP databases before incorporation, with quarterly re-screening and immediate EDD/refusal protocols triggered by any PEP, tax-crime, or high-risk jurisdiction matches; all Swift_LC and Wire_Transfer counterparties and issuing banks must be verified prior to share-capital deposit and first board authorization.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — lbr.lu — official portal of the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL) for company name reservation and e-formalities (RCS e-filing module)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be submitted in Latin script. French is the customary drafting language of the RCS, while French, German, and Luxembourgish are admissible under the trilingual regime; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin script. The name must be distinctive, physically and intellectually distinguishable from prior RCS entries, and must be accompanied by the legal-form indicator 'société à responsabilité limitée' or an unambiguous abbreviation such as 'SARL' or 'S.à r.l.'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: banque / bank (prior CSSF banking license required)
assurance / insurer / réassurance / reinsurance (prior Commissariat aux Assurances authorization)
fiduciaire / trust / trust company (regulated professional activity in Luxembourg)
audit / auditeur / réviseur (regulated statutory-audit professional title)
état / state / national / gouvernemental (prior ministerial authorization)
SICAV / SICAR / SPF / FCP (regulated collective-investment or private-wealth structures)
protected emblems (e.g., Croix-Rouge / Red Cross / Coat of Arms of Luxembourg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On RCSL refusal, the incorporator first receives the reasoned refusal; a corrected name may be resubmitted immediately via the LBR portal. If the ground is merely similarity, the applicant may obtain and file a written, legalized consent of the prior name holder. A formal written administrative request for review (recours gracieux) must be lodged with the RCSL within 30 days of refusal. Where the refusal is maintained, judicial recourse is available before the competent civil/commercial chamber of the Tribunal de Luxembourg within 3 months, assisted by Luxembourg counsel; parallel reservation of an alternative name is recommended to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Regulated domiciliation office acceptable at formation stage: a Luxembourg SARL must maintain a real registered office in Luxembourg, which may be supplied by a licensed domiciliation company. Pure virtual workspace without any local management will be considered deficient for the active operation of an ocean Ro-Ro shipping company; a discreet physical office in Luxembourg City with professional domiciliation services and local directors is the minimum benchmark for corporate tax residence and the Luxembourg shipping-register application.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 15% within the first 12 months after incorporation; approximately 35% by month 36, once VAT, payroll, and shipping-revenue books are activated and if the Luxembourg tax administration (Administration des contributions directes) conducts a substance or residence review.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS name reservation and availability certificate via LBR portal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RCSL/LBR tariff for name reservation and searches

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization bundle (corporate documents, good-standing certificate, UBO extract, powers of attorney, identity documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign issuing authorities and Luxembourg diplomatic/consular posts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular and apostille tariffs of the relevant states (per-document fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing and AML/KYC compliance file — PEP, EU/UN and OFAC sanctions screening, 25% UBO chain mapping, RBE declaration preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg compliance counsel (avocat à la Cour) and/or réviseur d'entreprises agréé
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Luxembourg AML/UBO onboarding services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of articles of association (statuts SARL), shareholders' agreements and pre-incorporation legal opinion
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Luxembourg corporate counsel (fixed fee for structures of standard complexity)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial act of incorporation (authentic form) and associated notarial attestations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory Luxembourg notarial tariffs and professional fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration (immatriculation) and RESA legal publication fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL) and Ministry of Justice (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RCSL/LBR and Ministry of Justice publication tariffs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: ISIC 5012 / ocean Ro-Ro car-carrier maritime licensing scoping — Luxembourg shipping register and EU maritime rules
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg maritime counsel and/or shipping consultancy
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Luxembourg maritime regulatory advice

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 710-1 et seq. governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); Luxembourg Business Registers and RCS registration rules; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) containing the articles of association, registered with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Standard SARL minimum capital is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up before RCS registration. Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked Luxembourg bank account in the company's name, and the bank certificate must be delivered to the notary; in-kind contributions require valuation by an approved statutory auditor when required by law. Disbursement is permitted only after legal personality is acquired through RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: the incorporator’s subscription to the entire issued share capital is approved; the paid-up capital remains deposited in the Company’s blocked Luxembourg bank account until RCS registration, and the Manager is authorized to release funds after registration within legal limits. RESOLVED: the registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg. The Manager is authorized to sign the lease, arrange bank and telecommunication services, and file RCS, RBE and public-administration registrations. RESOLVED: [Name] is appointed Manager (Gérant) with sole-signature power to represent the Company in Ro-Ro shipping contracts, charter agreements and port agency engagements. RESOLVED: the Company applies for maritime registration and environmental, classified-establishment, fire safety and occupational clearance permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital account and bank certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg commercial bank selected by the founders, acting for the SARL in formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the SARL en formation, deposit at least EUR 12,000 in cash, and instruct the bank to issue a blocking certificate addressed to the notary confirming that the funds are irrevocably reserved for the company's formation until release upon RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association or formation project
Proof of residential address of founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further AML/KYC clarification, provide the requested corporate and identity documentation promptly or escalate through the bank’s compliance department; if the bank unreasonably delays, open the account with another Luxembourg-regulated bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and authentication of the notarial incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) selected by the shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the bank blocking certificate, draft articles, identity documents, and registered-office consent to the notary. The notary verifies legal capacity, permitted corporate object, capital subscription and payment, then executes the notarial deed of incorporation and arranges subsequent electronic filing with the RCS.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate evidencing paid-up blocked capital
Valid passports or national identity cards of shareholders and managers
Landlord consent or lease agreement for the Luxembourg registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the bank identifies defects in the draft deed, execute a correcting addendum or re-execute the deed after rectification; any late submission is cured by renewed filing with the consent of all subscribers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and publication of legal personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After execution, the notary files the notarial deed and statutory data with the RCS through the LBR online filing portal. The company acquires legal personality upon RCS registration. The deed is published in the RESA in accordance with Luxembourg law.
required_dossiers: Identification data of managers and authorized signatories
RCS standard registration form completed by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or requires translation or correction, the notary responds through the LBR portal within the stated deadline, submits a rectified act, and re-files; if registration is refused, the founders may apply to the competent Luxembourg court for review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of beneficial ownership in the RBE register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after RCS registration, file the company's beneficial-owner data in the RBE, identifying every natural person directly or indirectly holding more than 25% of shares or voting rights, or controlling the company by other means. Attach certified identity documents and details of the control chain.
required_dossiers: List of beneficial owners with passport or national ID copies
Declaration of shareholding and control structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE filing is queried, verify the notarial ownership schedule, correct inconsistencies, and refile immediately; if the RBE rejects the filing, provide a formal clarification through the LBR helpdesk or engage legal counsel to submit the statutory declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate tax, VAT and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), Administration de l’Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), and Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, file the company for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax with the ACD, obtain a Luxembourg VAT number if the company will make taxable supplies, and register as an employer with the CCSS if the company will hire crew or shore staff. Use the MyGuichet and official e-filing portals.
required_dossiers: Description of business activity (ISIC 5012 — deep-sea Ro-Ro freight transport)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax administration requests additional data, respond in writing or through the company's tax representative; if a late registration penalty is assessed, submit a formal remission request and evidence of timely corporate formation steps.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Maritime operator registration and classified-establishment permit for shore premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Mobility and Public Works — Maritime Affairs Directorate; Administration de l’Environnement; competent commune for classified premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For operation of Ro-Ro vessels under Luxembourg flag or as a Luxembourg maritime operator, apply for ship registration and maritime operator authorization with the Maritime Affairs Directorate. For any shore office or ancillary facility meeting classified-establishment thresholds, file the classification notice with the commune and obtain the exploitation permit; coordinate environmental, fire-safety and occupational-inspection clearances.
required_dossiers: Tonnage certificate and ISM/ISPS documentation for vessels
Ownership or charter-party documentation for the Ro-Ro vessels
Lease, fire-safety certificate and workplace layout
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit application is queried, amend the operational or environmental compliance documents and resubmit; if the authority refuses the permit, invoke the internal-review procedure or appeal before the Administrative Tribunal within the applicable Luxembourg deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy, Direction of Industry; Ministry of Mobility and Public Works, Maritime Affairs Directorate; Administration de l’Environnement; and the competent municipal authority for classified establishments.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Classified Establishment Operating Permit (Autorisation d’exploitation d’établissement classé) and, where applicable, Luxembourg Maritime Register ship registration / maritime operator authorization for Ro-Ro vessel transport.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l’Environnement — Luxembourg Environment Agency, under the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration-tier / generally exempt for a representative office and Ro-Ro vessel operation without land-side terminals; full EIA Report required if the project includes a new Ro-Ro port terminal, ship repair yard, bunkering facility or other listed installation under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with MARPOL 73/78 Annexes I and VI, IMO global sulphur cap (0.50% m/m from 2020), NOx Tier III requirements in emission-control areas, EU MRV Regulation (EU) 2015/757, and applicable Luxembourg wastewater, VOC and waste-management standards for shore premises under Grand-Ducal implementing regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification for the registered office or leased shore premises issued by the competent commune; structural load inspection and workplace health-and-safety clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); and civil-defense no-objection for any premises designated as a classified establishment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct corporate income tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT, registration duties and estate duties; Administration des douanes et accises (Customs and Excise Administration) for export customs control. Unified taxpayer portal: MyGuichet.lu / eCDF (electronic tax filing service).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Luxembourg SARL: (1) incorporate the SARL via notarial deed before the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/LBR) and obtain registered address; (2) the 13-digit national identification number (numéro d'identification / matricule) is automatically generated at RCS registration and serves as the primary tax file reference; (3) apply to the AEDT for a Luxembourg VAT identification number in the form LU + 8 digits, after identifying the effective start date of taxable supplies and appointing if required a Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative for non-EU operators; (4) ensure real economic presence (local substance) including a Luxembourg office, board of managers, bank account, and statutory records; (5) activate e-access to MyGuichet/eCDF for electronic filing, payments, and official correspondence. A non-resident entity with no Luxembourg establishment performing taxable B2B telecommunication/digital services or cross-border supplies may register directly via the Mini One-Stop Shop/OSS without a local VAT number, while classic exports and imports require full clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not provide a US-style check-the-box entity classification election; an SARL is per se a taxable corporation for Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and municipal business tax. Available elections relevant to tax integration and VAT are: (a) fiscal unity election (intégration fiscale) among resident groups holding directly or indirectly at least 95% of the subsidiary’s shares and at least 95% of voting rights; (b) election to form a Luxembourg VAT group (assujetti unique) under Art. 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Act for financially, economically and organisationally interconnected resident persons; (c) limited option for partnerships to elect corporate taxation under Luxembourg domestic law, not applicable to an SARL; (d) hybrid and reverse-hybrid mismatch outcomes are not elective and are corrected mandatorily under Luxembourg’s implementation of ATAD 1/ATAD 2.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT/TVA — Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Mehrwertsteuer)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for resident taxable persons exercising the small business franchise exemption (assujetti obligatoire once threshold exceeded); non-established foreign suppliers have no general turnover threshold and must register from their first taxable transaction in Luxembourg; cross-border B2C digital and distance sales are handled through EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) procedures without requiring a Luxembourg domestic VAT ID.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg mandates electronic invoicing for B2G transactions through the PEPPOL network; there is no general real-time fiscal clearance, no continuous transaction control (CTC), no official digital stamping or API-based invoice clearance for domestic B2B transactions. VAT returns, recapitulative statements (EC sales lists), and Intrastat declarations must be filed electronically via MyGuichet/eCDF. Taxpayers must retain invoice files in a structured electronic format and Treasury/ERP integrations must support auditable XML/UBL/PEPPOL traces for cross-border and export transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Luxembourg VAT zero-rating applies to: (i) physical export of goods sold by the SARL to a non-EU customer where the goods leave the EU in unchanged state and the export is evidenced by a clearance-ready export declaration; and (ii) international deep-sea RoRo vehicle-carrier transport and directly related services (ocean freight, handling, lashing, port services, terminal charges) supplied for the direct needs of seagoing vessels on international routes to non-EU destinations, which qualify as international transport/services with full input VAT deduction. Services performed wholly within Luxembourg or domestic cabotage remain subject to the standard VAT rate. Eligibility requires valid commercial contracts, Bill of Lading, export packing list, proof of non-EU loading/discharge, and a demonstrable nexus between the invoiced supply and the international voyage.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / electronic export declaration with Movement Reference Number) accepted by Luxembourg Customs proving the physical exit of goods from the EU
Bill of Lading (RoRo ocean bill) evidencing that the vehicle-carrying vessel loaded at an EU port and discharged at a destination outside the EU

Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank SWIFT MT103 / bank credit confirmation showing export proceeds remitted from the non-resident charterer or buyer within the statutory settlement period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax and customs authorities may audit export zero-rating claims for the standard limitation period (5 years, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud or omission). If the export status is not substantiated with the required customs movement evidence, ocean Bill of Lading, and currency inward remittance proof, the supply is recharacterised as a taxable domestic supply and VAT at 17% is assessed, together with late interest. Administrative fines range from 10% to 100% of the undeclared VAT depending on gravity, while deliberate fraud may attract criminal penalties, imprisonment for managing officers, and unlimited joint liability for the VAT fiscal representative. Claimed export refunds are clawed back, input VAT credits on the export costs are disallowed, and customs records may be retrospectively invalidated for false or incomplete declarations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks (ESCB); prudential supervision of credit institutions and payment/e-money institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) under the amended Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector and the amended Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account operations. Luxembourg imposes no exchange-control licensing, no prior-authorisation requirement, and no transfer or remittance caps on cross-border flows. Equity injections, shareholder loans, freight receipts, profit distributions, and liquidation proceeds may be transferred freely. Operational constraints are limited to: (i) customer due diligence by credit institutions under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing; (ii) EU, UN, and Luxembourg sanctions screening; and (iii) BCL balance-of-payments statistical declaration requirements. Dividend and interest remittances to non-residents are subject to Luxembourg withholding tax (15% standard; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or an applicable double-tax treaty where conditions are met), but this does not require prior regulatory clearance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no mandatory surrender, compulsory conversion ratio, or statutory retention timeline for export proceeds. A Luxembourg SARL may retain deep-sea RoRo freight receivables in the invoicing currency (typically USD) in domestic or foreign bank accounts. The only overlay is the BCL external-statistics framework: resident non-bank entities must report cross-border transactions above the statutory threshold to the BCL on a monthly/quarterly basis, and the remitting bank will require a statistical purpose code (e.g., 'credits from exports of goods and services') at transaction execution.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (treasury centralisation) / Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Documentary Credit / Trade Finance Desk
Operational Account and Vessel-Financing / LC Facilities

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkees)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Structured Trade Finance

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium and ancillary only. Luxembourg-licensed e-money institutions and payment institutions under the amended Law of 10 November 2009 may provide payment accounts, SEPA/ISO 20022 credit transfers, and FX conversion, but are legally prohibited from granting credit, issuing or confirming commercial letters of credit, or acting as settlement banks. For a deep-sea RoRo carrier requiring documentary credits, vessel-escrow capacity, large freight-settlement liquidity, and ISDA-based hedging, a Tier-1 credit institution is mandatory. Passported EU EMIs can support ancillary collection flows (e.g., customer freight prepayments via SEPA instant credit transfers), but treasury centralisation, nostro relationships, and trade-finance rails must remain within a supervised banking group to satisfy CSSF substance and AML expectations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally expected for at least one director or a Luxembourg-resident authorised agent (e.g., fiduciary manager holding a notarised power of attorney) at the account-opening meeting on the bank's premises. Non-resident directors may complete identification through certified passport copies and notarised corporate resolutions; fully remote/video onboarding is accepted only for standard Low_Risk_Standard profiles, on a case-by-case basis, and is never available for escrow accounts or LC-issuing mandates. Original board resolutions appointing signatories, the current RCS excerpt, and the UBO declaration registered on the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (LBR) are uniformly required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-list exposure or embargoed-port destinations in charterparties or cargo itineraries (e.g., Russia, Iran, North Korea nexus, or high-risk flags of convenience)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written trade-compliance manual; constitutional sanctions clause in every charterparty; vessel AIS/IMO tracking logs; charterer and cargo-consignee LEI screening reports; denial-of-berth policy for sanctioned ports; certificate of good standing for shipowner and operating entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque UBO chain (nominee shareholders, discretionary trusts, unreported beneficial owners above 25%, or multi-tier holding structures)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised UBO declaration filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); notarised shareholders' register; corporate organisation chart; source-of-shares documentation; explanation of fiduciary agreements; proof of Luxembourg economic substance (office lease, payroll, Luxembourg-resident manager with executive powers).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unsubstantiated source of wealth for high-value vessel acquisition (eight-figure EUR/USD inflows to escrow)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vessel Sale and Purchase Agreement (Norwegian Saleform 2012); Bill of Sale; pre-purchase surveyor report; H&M insurance policy; P&I Club entry certificate; classification society certificate (e.g., Lloyd's Register, DNV); vessel-financing term sheet; confirmation of the lending bank's own AML file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors with no apparent nexus to Luxembourg and no local substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg substance file: amended articles of association; local domiciliation agreement; CV and mandate letter of local statutory director; payroll records and social-security filings; corporate income and net-wealth tax filings; treasury-management mandate appointing a Luxembourg-resident finance officer or fiduciary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large recurring USD freight receipts lacking matching trade documentation (money-laundering typology via charter revenue concealment)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transactional trail: signed charterparty; freight invoices cross-referenced to vessel IMO number and voyage number; port-authority invoices and disbursement vouchers; bank-statement reconciliation; ship-management reports; BCL balance-of-payments declaration reference numbers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound injections use SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 pacs.008. Equity contributions must be tagged with purpose code 'Capital Contribution / Direct Investment – Equity Capital' and supported by the notarised deed of contributions, RCS excerpt reflecting the share-capital increase, and the relevant notarised signatory resolution. Shareholder loans require a signed loan agreement, arm's-length interest rate, amortisation schedule, and tax-advice note on interest withholding exposure; the purpose code is 'Shareholder Loan – Direct Investment'; the receiving bank verifies remitter LEI/BIC, UBO names, contract reference, and tax classification before crediting the operational account. All inbound flows are simultaneously coded for BCL balance-of-payments statistics.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103/ISO 20022 pacs.008 via TARGET2 for EUR and via the bank's USD nostro network (e.g., CHIPS or correspondent bank) for USD, covering freight settlements, port disbursements, bunker payments, seafarer wages, and P&I premia. Trade-payment rail for vessel acquisition or heavy spares: commercial letters of credit issued by the Luxembourg bank (MT700), amendments (MT707), and reimbursement (MT756); required document set includes negotiable port-to-port Bill of Lading, commercial invoice, packing list, marine insurance certificate/P&I Blue Card, and vessel survey certificate. Intercompany treasury sweeps within the group use MT101 corporate-to-bank instructions with full audit trail referencing the underlying cash-pooling agreement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/NOK, EUR/JPY) matching deep-sea voyage revenue cycles, documented under the ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex (CSA) accepted by Luxembourg banks for shipping treasury centres.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with offshore-settlement restrictions (e.g., USD/CNY, USD/INR), concluded only through the bank's sanctioned-screened book and subject to EMIR transaction-reporting and clearing-threshold assessment.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (XCCYS) to convert USD-denominated freight income into EUR liabilities or align EUR-denominated vessel-financing debt with operating-currency exposure, subject to EMIR reporting and mandatory central clearing above the non-financial-counterparty clearing threshold.

Plain-vanilla European FX options, collars, and basis swaps used for voyage-cycle hedging of USD freight revenue with maturity capped at 24 months, with margin or collateral posting per the bank's ISDA CSA and internal credit-limit framework.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (financial statements) filing with trade register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS Luxembourg), filed electronically through MyGuichet
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the balance-sheet date; annual general meeting must be held within six months of financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers formal warning, monetary penalties under the Companies Act, and after persistent default potential court-ordered strike-off or dissolution; directors' liability for continued non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) via Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the calendar month following the anniversary of initial RBE registration; shareholding or control changes must be declared within 30 days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm or update triggers administrative fines and daily penalties, potential criminal sanctions under the Beneficial Owners Act, and blockage of profit distributions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined annual corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) via MyTax / eCDF
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the calendar year following the financial year-end for calendar-year SARLs; available extensions apply only through ACD e-filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs default interest per month, late-payment surcharges, provisional tax assessments on available facts, and administrative enforcement measures; annual minimum net wealth tax remains payable.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit by an agréé réviseur d'entreprises is compulsory if, for two consecutive financial years, the SARL exceeds at least two of: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average number of employees 50; audit may also be required by shareholders holding qualifying interests.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2016 implementing Directive 2013/34/EU; optional application of IFRS for annual statutory accounts, mandatory IFRS for consolidated accounts of issuers listed on a regulated EU market

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each SARL must maintain an up-to-date Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs); the registered data must be confirmed annually in the month after the RBE anniversary date, and share transfers or control changes must be reported within 30 days. An RBE declaration must be completed before any dividend or transfer can be validly authorised.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (register of shareholders and transfers)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 1,800–3,200 typical annual registered-office/domiciliation and professional corporate-services fee
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 7,500–22,000 typical certified audit fee for an active deep-sea Ro-Ro carrier SARL, dependent on balance-sheet size and related-entity consolidation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% for taxable income exceeding EUR 175,000; 15% for the first EUR 175,000; plus 7% unemployment fund solidarity surcharge on CIT and municipal business tax at the commune-applicable rate (Luxembourg City 6.75%), producing an aggregate headline rate of approximately 24.94% for a Luxembourg City SARL.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Optional tonnage tax regime for qualifying ocean-going Ro-Ro vessel operations based on net tonnage replacing normal CIT, municipal business tax and net wealth tax on shipping profits; participation exemption regime granting 95% exemption on qualifying dividend and capital gains income; various accelerated depreciation rules for vessel assets.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiry; no carryback permitted)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 1 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités et l'impôt commercial communal) filed electronically via the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration e-CDF portal (Espace e-Déclaration des sociétés).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal year; normally calendar year unless authorized otherwise).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: By 31 December of the calendar year immediately following the fiscal year-end; extensions may be granted on justified request to the competent local tax office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss before income tax from the statutory financial statements (résultat net comptable).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for every Luxembourg-resident SARL, irrespective of the residence of shareholders. Non-resident shareholders do not file on behalf of the company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses to be reintegrated (fines, 50% of client entertainment expenses, certain taxes, and other statutorily disallowed costs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete from the SARL's own books; no direct non-resident shareholder input.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income deductible from account profit, notably participation-exempt dividends and shipping profits covered by the optional tonnage tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Substantiate exemption claims with ownership certificates, holding period evidence, and tonnage tax election documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforward utilisation (prior assessed losses offset against current-year taxable income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only usable if the Luxembourg tax administration has formally recognised the carryforward; ensure historical loss assessments are retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income base (base imposable) after application of accounting adjustments, deductibles, and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the central tax base for each Luxembourg resident SARL; no apportionment to non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Comprehensive tax computation showing corporate income tax at 15%/17%, solidarity surcharge at 7%, and communal business tax at the municipal rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax authorities calculate the final assessment; the SARL remains solely liable for the declared tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative penalty of up to EUR 75,000 in serious cases and default interest of 0.8% per month on unpaid taxes; the tax office may issue an ex officio assessment on an estimated basis, and concealment leading to under-assessment can attract criminal fines (up to EUR 1,000,000) and imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% under domestic Luxembourg law (0% under the Luxembourg participation exemption / EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the non-resident parent holds at least 10% for a minimum 12-month holding period or acquisition cost threshold of EUR 1.2 million).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate at source, the paying Luxembourg SARL must collect and retain: (i) a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the shareholder's country of residence; (ii) a statement of beneficial ownership; and (iii) evidence of shareholding and holding period. The corporate withholding tax declaration is filed electronically via the e-CDF portal, and any excess WHT withheld at 15% may be reclaimed by the non-resident shareholder through a refund application to the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The Luxembourg domestic statutory rate for interest and royalties paid by a resident commercial SARL is generally 0% (no withholding tax source levy); accordingly most Luxembourg income tax treaties assign full source-state taxing rights to the recipient's residence state, with treaty rates frequently 0% for royalties and 0%/10% for interest, subject to OSTC-compliant beneficial ownership.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue triggers mandatory Country-by-Country Reporting, Master File and Local File obligations; entities below the threshold must still prepare and maintain contemporaneous arm's length documentation upon request by the Luxembourg tax authorities, covering all cross-border related-party transactions (charter hire, management fees, intercompany debt).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg is not an Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) jurisdiction in the offshore sense, but imposes robust substance requirements through GAAR, ATAD anti-abuse rules, beneficial ownership case law, and administrative circulars. A Luxembourg SARL operating an ocean Ro-Ro vessel fleet must demonstrate actual management and decision-making in Luxembourg (board meetings, operational control, strategic chartering decisions, accounting substance) to secure tax residence, treaty benefits, and tonnage tax eligibility; artificial brass-plate arrangements may be disregarded by the tax administration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of freight revenues from Ro-Ro car carrier voyages, use of fictitious invoices for vessel operating costs, or false substitution of taxable shipping income with non-existent expenses in the Luxembourg Formulaire 1 filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of understated tax plus default interest at 0.8% per month; administrative penalties up to 10%–25% of evaded tax; criminal prosecution for tax fraud with fines up to EUR 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause the filing of knowingly false returns may be held jointly and severally liable for the company's underpaid tax; criminal conviction may result in imprisonment, disqualification from managing Luxembourg entities, and travel restrictions imposed by the Luxembourg courts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Relying on a Luxembourg SARL with no physical office, no staff, no operational control, and no real economic activity in Luxembourg solely to attract treaty benefits or the tonnage tax regime while the vessel and commercial management remain in a high-tax or non-treaty jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Luxembourg tax administration may disregard the entity under the general anti-abuse rule (abus de droit), deny the tax residence certificate, reject the tonnage tax election, apply full normal taxation, and impose non-filing/delinquency penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and statutory bodies participating in the sham arrangement may incur civil restitution for denied tax benefits; where misrepresentation is found to be fraudulent, criminal sanctions including imprisonment and personal monetary penalties up to EUR 100,000 can apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany time charter hire, vessel management fees, and shareholder loan interest at non-arm's length levels; failing to prepare or present transfer pricing documentation during a Luxembourg tax audit on Ro-Ro vessel transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Authoritative upward tax adjustment to the arm's length profit; a specific transfer pricing surcharge of up to 10% of the adjustment; late payment interest; and where documentation is absent, an additional penalty possible under the Luxembourg General Tax Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in or approve artificial pricing structures can be personally assessed for the resulting tax deficiency under liability rules applicable to wilfully negligent managers; severe cases may attract criminal tax fraud sanctions and director disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify and register the ultimate beneficial owners of the Luxembourg SARL with the Luxembourg Business Registers; obstructing bank due-diligence queries on SWIFT LC and wire-transfer payment chains involving vessel charter payments; failing to report suspicion of money laundering or sanctions evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines for failure to file or maintain the beneficial ownership register (up to EUR 125,000 for serious breaches), with possible public disclosure orders; AML law violations may also carry imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 5 million depending on the professional status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and ultimate shareholders can be prosecuted for money laundering and beneficial ownership concealment; courts may impose custodial sentences, travel bans, freeze orders on personal assets, and civil compensation to affected parties.
